title: Smooth, globally Polyak-Łojasiewicz functions are nonlinear least-squares
summary: The Polyak-Łojasiewicz (PŁ) condition is often invoked in nonconvex optimization because it allows fast convergence of algorithms beyond strong convexity. A function $f \colon \mathcal{M} \to \mathbb{R}$ on a Riemannian manifold $\mathcal{M}$ is globally PŁ if $\|\nabla f(x)\|^2 \geq 2μ(f(x) - f^*)$ for all $x$, where $f^* = \inf f$ and $μ> 0$. How much does this pointwise, first-order inequality constrain $f$ and its set of minimizers $S$?
